- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for mean reversion or sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day average is rising.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.00 → 0.67), model lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.
- Avoid forecasting based solely on recent 18-day history; incorporate sentiment lag (e.g., 3–5 days prior sentiment) to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
